t: The southern kingdom of the Israelites, ruled from Jerusalem by kings of the House of David for about 340 years.
It survived as a vassal of Assyria, Egypt and Babylon, resisting Sennacherib’s invasion of 701 BCE.
Nebuchadnezzar II destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 587 BCE; the exile shaped Judaism and the Hebrew Bible.
dyk: The Siloam tunnel under Jerusalem, over 500 metres long, was dug from both ends; an inscription records the moment the two teams of diggers met.
ev: The kingdom of Solomon splits; Rehoboam keeps Judah and Jerusalem
Ahaz becomes a vassal of Tiglath-pileser III of Assyria
Sennacherib invades Judah, takes Lachish and besieges Jerusalem
Josiah’s religious reform centralises worship in Jerusalem
Josiah is killed at Megiddo confronting the pharaoh Necho II
Nebuchadnezzar II captures Jerusalem and deports Jehoiachin
Jerusalem and the temple are destroyed; the elite are exiled to Babylon
